summary: Design Swiggy at the scale of ~150 K restaurant partners, 4.5 L+ delivery partners, and 2 M+ daily orders across 500+ Indian cities: food delivery with driver dispatch (Swiggy's "Dispatch 2.0" auto-assignment), live order…

sections.title: Step 1: Clarify Requirements (5 min)
sections.body:
> **In one line:** Design Swiggy at the scale of ~150 K restaurant partners, 4.5 L+ delivery partners, and 2 M+ daily orders across 500+ Indian cities: food delivery with **driver dispatch** (Swiggy's "Dispatch 2.0" auto-assignment), **live order tracking**, **queue management during peak dinner windows** (order batching at cloud kitchens), **partner/restaurant app**, and **Swiggy Instamart** (10-min grocery). Focus on the **batched dispatch algorithm** (one rider, multiple pickups/dropoffs), **cloud-kitchen queue fairness**, and the **Kafka + Geospatial (H3 + Redis GEO)** backbone. ---

### Functional Requirements
- **Restaurant discovery & ordering**: similar to Zomato — search, menu, cart, place order.
- **Order lifecycle**: `placed → restaurant_accepted → preparing → ready_for_pickup → picked_up → en_route → delivered` (plus `cancelled`).
- **Dispatch — auto-assignment**: Swiggy uses auto-assignment (not rider-pickup). The system picks a rider and assigns; rider has 15 s to acknowledge, else reassign.
- **Batched dispatch**: a single rider can carry up to 3 orders if pickups/dropoffs are along a similar route — reduces cost & delivery time. Swiggy calls this "multi-order dispatch".
- **Cloud kitchen queues**: a single kitchen (Swiggy Access) hosts 10+ brand menus; orders queue by brand; kitchen display system (KDS) routes each item to the right station; FIFO + priority lanes for high-value orders.
- **Live tracking**: rider GPS streamed every 5 s to user & restaurant apps; ETA recomputed live.
- **Instamart (10-min grocery)**: dark stores with pre-positioned inventory; rider pre-assigned to dark-store zone; order picked within 2 min of placement.
- **Rider app**: go-online, accept assignment, navigate, mark delivered, earnings dashboard.
- **Restaurant app**: accept orders, KDS view, mark ready, update stock.
- **Swiggy One membership**: free delivery + no surge for subscribers (separate serviceability logic).
- **Payments**: UPI, cards, wallets, COD, Swiggy Money (wallet).
- **Ratings & reviews**: post-delivery ratings (food, delivery, packaging).

### Non-Functional Requirements
- **Availability** 99.95% for order pipeline, 99.9% for discovery.
- **Latency**: discovery p99 < 300 ms; order placement p99 < 1 s; rider location update p99 < 500 ms; auto-assignment p99 < 5 s (from `ready_for_pickup` to rider assigned).
- **Scale**: 2 M orders/day, 4.5 L riders (250 K online at peak), 150 K restaurants, 500 cities.
- **Throughput**: ~15 K orders/min at peak dinner (7–9 PM); ~80 K rider pings/s; ~5 K KDS updates/s.
- **Storage**: 2 M orders/day × 25 KB metadata = 50 GB/day metadata; GPS tracks ~2 MB/order = 4 TB/day. 5-year retention.
- **Geospatial**: rider-position queries (`GEORADIUS` < 50 ms) and restaurant catalog queries (`geo_distance` < 100 ms).
- **Consistency**: strong for order state machine (single owner); eventual for rider position (5 s lag acceptable); strong for KDS item-state transitions (no double-pickup).
- **Multi-region**: all data in India (data residency); active-active across Mumbai + Delhi NCR DCs.

### Back-of-Envelope Estimation
- **Orders/day**: 2 M; peak dinner ~3× avg = 7 K orders/min during 7–9 PM.
- **Rider pings**: 250 K online × 1 ping/5 s = 50 K pings/s.
- **Auto-assignments**: 7 K/min = ~120/s peak; each assignment evaluates ~30 candidates → ~3.6 K scoring ops/s.
- **Batched orders**: ~25% of orders are batched (2 orders per rider on average); saves ~15% rider-miles.
- **Storage**: orders 50 GB/day; GPS 4 TB/day; ratings 20 GB/day; 5-year total ~9 PB.
- **Instamart**: ~3 L orders/day, average ticket size ₹250; dark stores ~500 nationwide; each dark store serves ~600 orders/day.
- **KDS event volume**: 5 K updates/s × 30 s average prep = ~150 K active item-states.

### Scope
- **In scope**: ordering, auto-assignment dispatch, batched dispatch, cloud-kitchen queue, live tracking, scaling, multi-region, Instamart variant.
- **Out of scope**: Swiggy Genie (point-to-point pickup), Swiggy HDFC credit card, marketing/CRM, fraud ML (mention only), full maps/routing (use Mapbox/OSM), recommendation engine (black box).

sections.title: Step 2: High-Level Architecture (10 min)
sections.body:
### Components 1. **DNS + CDN** (Route 53 + CloudFront/Akamai) — routes apps to nearest API region, serves images. 2. **API Gateway** (Envoy/Kong) — TLS, JWT, rate limiting, request routing, mobile BFF. 3. **Microservices**: - **User service**: profile, addresses, Swiggy One membership. - **Restaurant service**: restaurant catalog, serviceability, hours. - **Menu service**: structured menus, stock, pricing, add-ons. - **Discovery service**: Elasticsearch geo_point + function_score ranking. - **Order service**: state machine; publishes `order-events`. - **Dispatch service**: auto-assignment + batched dispatch; the core algorithm. - **Geolocation service**: rider live positions in Redis GEO; H3 cell routing. - **Rider service**: rider profile, vehicle, status, earnings, onboarding. - **ETA service**: predicts prep time + rider travel time; ML (XGBoost + road graph). - **Pricing service**: bill calculation, GST, surge, Swiggy One waivers. - **KDS service** (cloud kitchen): item-state machine, station routing, queue fairness. - **Payment service**: UPI/cards/wallets via Razorpay/Juspay; Swiggy Money ledger. - **Rating service**: post-delivery ratings, moderation. - **Notification service**: FCM/APNS push, SMS, WhatsApp. 4. **Geospatial index** — Redis GEO for riders (live), Elasticsearch geo_point for restaurants, H3 hexagons (level 8) for cell routing and surge. 5. **Kafka** — event backbone. Topics: `order-events`, `rider-location`, `restaurant-events`, `kds-events`, `payment-events`. 6. **Cassandra** — orders metadata, GPS tracks, ratings. 7. **MySQL/Aurora** — restaurants, menus, payments, partner ledger, restaurant master. 8. **Redis** — rider positions, surge cache, menu cache, KDS active state, session cart. 9. **Elasticsearch** — restaurant search & dish search. 10. **ClickHouse** — analytics warehouse (GMV, SLA breach, partner performance). 11. **WebSocket gateway** — streams rider location to user & restaurant apps. 12. **Mapbox/Google Maps** — routing, ETA baseline, map tiles. ### Mermaid Diagram ```mermaid flowchart LR U([User App]) --> DNS[Route 53 + CDN] RP([Restaurant App]) --> DNS DP([Rider App]) --> DNS DNS --> GW[API Gateway + WS] GW --> USVC[User svc] GW --> RSVC[Restaurant svc] GW --> MSVC[Menu svc] GW --> DISC[Discovery svc] GW --> ORD[Order svc] GW --> WSGW[WebSocket GW] GW --> PAY[Payment svc] WSGW --> U WSGW --> RP WSGW --> DP DP -->|ping every 5s| LOC[Geolocation svc] LOC --> GEO[(Redis GEO
rider index)] LOC --> K2[(Kafka: rider-location)] DISC --> ES[(Elasticsearch geo)] DISC --> MREDIS[(Redis menu cache)] U -->|place order| ORD ORD --> K1[(Kafka: order-events)] K1 --> DISP[Dispatch svc] DISP --> GEO DISP --> ETA[ETA svc] DISP --> RSVC2[Rider svc] RSVC2 -->|assign + 15s ack| DP DP -->|ack| RSVC2 RSVC2 --> ORD K1 --> PAY K1 --> NOTIF[Notification svc] K1 --> AN[(ClickHouse analytics)] K1 --> KDS[KDS svc
cloud kitchen] KDS --> KDSR[(Redis KDS state)] KDS --> RP K2 --> MM[Map matching] K2 --> SURGE[Delivery surge svc] SURGE --> SC[(Redis surge cache)] PAY --> PG[(Razorpay/Juspay)] PAY --> DB[(MySQL payments)] ORD --> CASS[(Cassandra orders + GPS)] ``` ### ASCII Diagram ``` +-------------------+ +-------------------+ +-------------------+ | User App | | Restaurant App | | Rider App | | (browse, order) | | (accept, KDS) | | (ping, deliver) | +---+-----------+---+ +---+-----------+---+ +---+-----------+---+ | | | | | | REST | | WS | REST | WS | ping | WS v v v v v v +-----+-----------+--------------+-----------+--------------+-----------+--+ | API Gateway / WS Gateway (per region) | +--+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+-----+ | | | | | | | | | | | | v v v v v v v v v v v v +------+--+ ++ +--+---+ ++ +--+---+ ++ +--+--+ ++ +--+--+ ++ +--+--+ ++ +-----+ |User | |Menu| |Rest.| |Disc.| |Order| |Rider| |Pay | |Notif| |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | |svc | +--------+ +----+ +-----+ +--+--+ +--+--+ +-----+ +----+ +-----+ | | | v v v +---+---+ +--+----+ +-+------+ | Elastic| |Dispatch| |Razorpay| |search | |svc | |gateway | |(geo) | +--+--+--+ +--------+ +--------+ | | ^ | | | +----+ +----+ | v v +---+----+--+ +-----+--------+ |Redis GEO | |Redis GEO | |restaurants| |live riders | +----------+ +-------------+ ^ | (rider pings every 5s) Order state machine: placed -> restaurant_accepted -> preparing -> ready_for_pickup -> picked_up -> en_route -> delivered Auto-assignment flow (Dispatch 2.0): ready_for_pickup -> dispatch picks rider -> 15s ack -> assigned -> picked_up ``` ### Request Flow Walkthrough 1. **User opens app**: `GET /api/v1/discovery?lat&lon&q=` → discovery service queries Elasticsearch `geo_distance` + `function_score`; results cached in Redis `cell:{h3}` TTL 5 min. 2. **User places order**: `POST /api/v1/orders` → order service validates cart, computes bill (pricing service), reserves payment, persists order in Cassandra `placed`, publishes `order-placed` to Kafka. 3. **Restaurant accepts**: partner app receives push; on accept → `restaurant_accepted`. If cloud kitchen, KDS service creates an item-state row per dish and routes to station. ETA service recomputes. 4. **Auto-assignment (Dispatch 2.0)**: when order transitions to `preparing`, dispatch service is triggered. It computes pickup ETA, queries Redis GEO for online riders within ~2.5 km, scores them by (ETA, on-time %, idle time, batch compatibility), picks the best, sends assignment via WebSocket. Rider has 15 s to acknowledge. If no ack → reassign next-best. No "reject" — auto-assignment is binding (the rider can only request unassignment for documented reasons). 5. **Batched dispatch**: if the rider already has 1 active pickup nearby (< 1 km, similar drop-off direction), dispatch may add a second order to the same rider. Cap = 3 orders/rider. 6. **Cloud kitchen KDS**: KDS routes items to stations (e.g. "North Indian station", "Chinese station"). Each station sees a FIFO queue; high-value orders get a priority lane (weighted fair queueing). State: `queued → cooking → plated → ready`. 7. **Pickup & delivery**: rider navigates (Mapbox), marks `picked_up` (requires OTP for high-value), then `en_route` → `delivered`. Rider location streamed via WebSocket every 5 s. 8. **Surge**: surge service consumes `order-placed` + `rider-online`, computes per H3 cell, writes `surge:{h3}` TTL 5 min.

sections.title: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
sections.body:
### Tables / Schema

**MySQL — `restaurants`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE restaurants (
    restaurant_id      BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    name               VARCHAR(200),
    chain_id           BIGINT,
    kitchen_id         BIGINT,        -- NULL for standalone; set for cloud-kitchen brands
    cuisine_tags       JSON,
    lat                DECIMAL(10,7),
    lon                DECIMAL(10,7),
    city_id            INT,
    avg_rating         DECIMAL(3,2),
    is_active          BOOLEAN,
    delivery_enabled   BOOLEAN,
    is_instamart       BOOLEAN,        -- dark store flag
    created_at         TIMESTAMP,
    INDEX idx_kitchen (kitchen_id),
    INDEX idx_city_active (city_id, is_active)
);
```

**MySQL — `menu_items`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE menu_items (
    item_id            BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    restaurant_id      BIGINT,
    name               VARCHAR(200),
    price              DECIMAL(8,2),
    is_veg             BOOLEAN,
    in_stock           BOOLEAN,
    station            VARCHAR(50),    -- for KDS routing in cloud kitchens
    prep_time_s        INT,            -- median prep time
    INDEX idx_restaurant (restaurant_id)
);
```

**Cassandra — `orders`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id           UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id            UUID,
    restaurant_id      UUID,
    rider_id           UUID,
    batch_id           UUID,           -- shared by batched orders
    pickup_lat         DOUBLE,
    pickup_lon         DOUBLE,
    drop_lat           DOUBLE,
    drop_lon           DOUBLE,
    status             TEXT,
    items              TEXT,
    subtotal           DECIMAL,
    delivery_fee       DECIMAL,
    taxes              DECIMAL,
    discount           DECIMAL,
    total              DECIMAL,
    surge_mult         DOUBLE,
    payment_method     TEXT,
    placed_at          TIMESTAMP,
    delivered_at       TIMESTAMP
);
```

**Cassandra — `order_tracking`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE order_tracking (
    order_id    UUID,
    ts          TIMESTAMP,
    lat         DOUBLE,
    lon         DOUBLE,
    heading     DOUBLE,
    speed       DOUBLE,
    rider_id    UUID,
    PRIMARY KEY (order_id, ts)
) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (ts ASC);
```

**Cassandra — `orders_by_user`** (denormalised for "my orders")
```sql
CREATE TABLE orders_by_user (
    user_id      UUID,
    placed_at    TIMESTAMP,
    order_id     UUID,
    status       TEXT,
    restaurant_id UUID,
    total        DECIMAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, placed_at)
) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (placed_at DESC);
```

**Redis — KDS active state** (per cloud kitchen)
```
HSET kds:{kitchen_id}:active {item_state_id}  {json: order_id, station, state, enqueued_at}
ZADD kds:{kitchen_id}:queue:{station}  {ts}  {item_state_id}
```

**Redis GEO — `riders:online:{city}`**
```
GEOADD riders:online:bangalore 77.5946 12.9716 "rider_42"
GEORADIUS riders:online:bangalore 77.5946 12.9716 2.5 km COUNT 30 ASC WITHCOORD WITHDIST
```

### Indexes
- MySQL `restaurants`: (city_id, is_active), (kitchen_id).
- Elasticsearch `restaurants`: `geo_point` field, `bool` filters (cuisine/veg/instamart), `function_score` for ranking.
- Cassandra: PK on `order_id`; denormalised `orders_by_user` for user-history queries.
- Redis GEO: sorted set on geohash; O(log N + M) radius scan.
- Redis KDS: a hash for active item-states and a per-station sorted set (FIFO by enqueue timestamp; priority lanes use a separate sorted set with priority score).

### Storage Choice
- **Cassandra** for orders & tracking: write-heavy, time-series, multi-region.
- **MySQL** for restaurants/menus/payments: ACID, rich indexes, moderate write rate.
- **Elasticsearch** for discovery: rich geo + ranking + full-text.
- **Redis** for live rider positions, surge cache, menu cache, KDS active state.
- **S3 + CloudFront** for images.
- **ClickHouse** for analytics (columnar, fast aggregations over billions of order rows).

sections.title: Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- Lower = better.
- Check if new pickup/drop aligns with rider's existing route.
- Priority 1 = normal, 2 = high-value, 3 = bulk/catering (slightly lower).
- Pickup must be within max_extra_km of an existing pickup
- Drop-off direction must roughly align (dot product on unit vectors)
- (simplified — real impl uses routing-graph ETA)
- Escalate: widen radius or broadcast
- Weighted fair queueing: priority 2 orders advance ~2x faster

**Defines:** `haversine_km()`, `find_candidate_riders()`, `score_rider()`, `is_batchable()`, `auto_assign()`, `enqueue_item()`, `pop_next()`

### API Design
```
GET  /api/v1/discovery?lat&lon&q&cuisine&veg&sort&page
GET  /api/v1/restaurants/{id}/menu
POST /api/v1/orders                          {cart, address_id, payment_method, coupon}
GET  /api/v1/orders/{id}
GET  /api/v1/orders/{id}/track
WS   /ws/v1/track/{order_id}
POST /api/v1/rider/online
POST /api/v1/rider/location                  {lat, lon, heading, speed}
POST /api/v1/rider/assignment/{id}/ack
POST /api/v1/restaurants/{id}/orders/{order_id}/accept
POST /api/v1/restaurants/{id}/orders/{order_id}/ready
GET  /api/v1/kds/{kitchen_id}/station/{station}/queue
POST /api/v1/kds/{kitchen_id}/item/{item_state_id}/transition   {to_state}
```

### Key Algorithms

**Auto-assignment with batched dispatch**
```python
import heapq, math

def haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):
    R = 6371.0
    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)
    dphi = math.radians(lat2 - lat1)
    dlmb = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)
    a = math.sin(dphi/2)**2 + math.cos(p1)*math.cos(p2)*math.sin(dlmb/2)**2
    return 2 * R * math.asin(math.sqrt(a))

def find_candidate_riders(redis_geo, city, pickup_lat, pickup_lon,
                          radius_km=2.5, limit=30):
    raw = redis_geo.georadius(
        f"riders:online:{city}", pickup_lon, pickup_lat, radius_km,
        unit="km", withcoord=True, withdist=True, count=limit, sort="ASC")
    return [{
        "rider_id": r[0].decode(),
        "dist_km":  r[1],
        "lat":      r[2][1],
        "lon":      r[2][0],
    } for r in raw]

def score_rider(rider, pickup_lat, pickup_lon, eta_lookup, rider_stats,
                active_load):
    """Lower = better. Penalise high load; reward idle + on-time."""
    eta_min = eta_lookup(rider["rider_id"], rider["lat"], rider["lon"],
                         pickup_lat, pickup_lon)
    on_time = rider_stats.get(rider["rider_id"], {}).get("on_time_pct", 0.9)
    idle_min = rider_stats.get(rider["rider_id"], {}).get("idle_min", 5)
    load = active_load.get(rider["rider_id"], 0)        # 0..3 active orders
    return (eta_min * (1 + 0.3 * load)        # 30% ETA penalty per existing order
            + (1 - on_time) * 20.0
            + max(0, 10 - idle_min) * 0.1)

def is_batchable(new_order, rider_active_orders, max_extra_km=1.5, max_orders=3):
    """Check if new pickup/drop aligns with rider's existing route."""
    if len(rider_active_orders) >= max_orders:
        return False
    for o in rider_active_orders:
        # pickup must be within max_extra_km of an existing pickup
        if haversine_km(new_order["pickup_lat"], new_order["pickup_lon"],
                        o["pickup_lat"], o["pickup_lon"]) > max_extra_km:
            return False
        # drop-off direction must roughly align (dot product on unit vectors)
        # (simplified — real impl uses routing-graph ETA)
    return True

def auto_assign(redis_geo, city, order, eta_lookup, rider_stats,
                active_load, rider_orders, assigner, ack_timeout_s=15):
    candidates = find_candidate_riders(redis_geo, city,
                                       order["pickup_lat"], order["pickup_lon"])
    scored = [(score_rider(c, order["pickup_lat"], order["pickup_lon"],
                           eta_lookup, rider_stats, active_load), c)
              for c in candidates]
    heapq.heapify(scored)
    for _ in range(3):                  # up to 3 attempts
        if not scored:
            return None
        _, rider = heapq.heappop(scored)
        batchable = is_batchable(order, rider_orders.get(rider["rider_id"], []))
        ok = assigner.assign(rider["rider_id"], order["order_id"],
                             ack_timeout_s=ack_timeout_s, batchable=batchable)
        if ok:                          # ack received
            return rider
    # escalate: widen radius or broadcast
    return None
```

**Cloud-kitchen KDS — weighted fair queueing per station**
```python
def enqueue_item(kds_redis, kitchen_id, station, item_state_id, priority=1):
    """Priority 1 = normal, 2 = high-value, 3 = bulk/catering (slightly lower)."""
    import time
    ts = time.time()
    # weighted fair queueing: priority 2 orders advance ~2x faster
    score = ts * (1.0 / priority)
    kds_redis.zadd(f"kds:{kitchen_id}:queue:{station}", {item_state_id: score})
    kds_redis.hset(f"kds:{kitchen_id}:active", item_state_id,
                   f'{{"station":"{station}","state":"queued","ts":{ts}}}')

def pop_next(kds_redis, kitchen_id, station):
    item = kds_redis.zpopmin(f"kds:{kitchen_id}:queue:{station}")
    if not item:
        return None
    item_state_id, _ = item[0]
    kds_redis.hset(f"kds:{kitchen_id}:active", item_state_id,
                   f'{{"station":"{station}","state":"cooking"}}')
    return item_state_id.decode()
```

sections.title: Step 5: Scalability & Reliability (5 min)
sections.body:
### Scaling Challenges
- **Dinner peak (7–9 PM)**: 3× normal QPS. Autoscale stateless services (HPA on CPU + QPS). Pre-warm caches (popular restaurants, menus) at 6 PM. Over-provision dispatch workers (HPA on Kafka lag for `order-events`).
- **Geospatial index hot spots**: a single Redis GEO key per city gets hammered. Shard by H3 hexagon (level 8, ~0.7 km²) — `riders:online:{city}:{h3}`. Cross-cell dispatch scans neighbouring H3 cells.
- **Rider location write fan-in**: 50 K pings/s. Use Redis Cluster (16 shards) + pipelined writes. Kafka spout for durability; ingestion consumer batches writes (every 100 ms).
- **Batched dispatch complexity**: scoring with active-load + route-alignment is expensive. Cache `rider_active_orders` in Redis; precompute pairwise distances for hot zones.
- **KDS fairness under peak**: cloud kitchens can receive 1 000 orders/hr during dinner. Weighted fair queueing (priority lanes) prevents high-value orders from being starved by long FIFO queues. Station-level autoscaling (add staff) triggered when queue depth > threshold for 5 min.
- **Multi-region active-active**: orders placed in Mumbai DC stay in Mumbai; Delhi NCR DC serves northern cities. Cassandra `NetworkTopologyStrategy` RF=3 per DC. Cross-region only for restaurant master data via Kafka MirrorMaker2.

### Caching Strategy
- **Restaurant list by H3 cell**: Redis `cell:{h3_id}:restaurants` TTL 5 min (with jitter ± 60 s to avoid stampede). Cache-aside + single-flight on miss.
- **Menu**: Redis `menu:{restaurant_id}` TTL 60 s; invalidated by Kafka `restaurant-events`.
- **Rider live position**: Redis GEO (in-memory).
- **Surge**: Redis `surge:{h3_id}` TTL 5 min.
- **KDS active state**: Redis hash + sorted sets; persisted to Cassandra every 30 s for durability.
- **Discovery results**: CDN edge-cache for popular searches, 30 s TTL.

### Failure Modes
- **Rider doesn't ack in 15 s**: dispatch moves to the next-best candidate. If 3 attempts fail, widen radius (2.5 → 4 km) then broadcast with a bonus.
- **No rider available (supply crisis)**: surge spikes (auto-cap 2.5×); orders with ETA > 60 min get a "high demand" warning at checkout; very long waits (8 min) auto-cancel + refund.
- **Restaurant partner offline**: 90-second accept SLA; if no accept, auto-cancel + refund; fall back to auto-accept for opted-in chains.
- **Redis GEO down**: fallback to Elasticsearch `geo_distance` query (slower but durable); degraded mode flag.
- **Cassandra quorum failure**: order writes circuit-break to 503; active-active failover to other DC; client retries with backoff.
- **Payment gateway timeout**: idempotency key prevents double-charge; reconcile via webhook + nightly batch.
- **Kafka broker loss**: RF=3 covers; producers retry on `LEADER_NOT_AVAILABLE`.
- **KDS Redis loss**: fall back to per-station in-memory queue in the KDS service pod; reconcile from Kafka event log on recovery.
- **Mapbox outage**: ETA service falls back to haversine distance ÷ avg city speed; routing returns cached polyline.

diagram.title: Step 5: Scalability & Reliability (5 min) — step by step

steps.label: Scaling Challenges
steps.narration: Dinner peak (7–9 PM): 3× normal QPS. Autoscale stateless services (HPA on CPU + QPS).

steps.label: Caching Strategy
steps.narration: Restaurant list by H3 cell: Redis cell:{h3_id}:restaurants TTL 5 min (with jitter ± 60 s to avoid stampede). Cache-aside + single-flight on miss.

steps.label: Failure Modes
steps.narration: Rider doesn't ack in 15 s: dispatch moves to the next-best candidate. If 3 attempts fail, widen radius (2.5 → 4 km) then broadcast with a bonus.

quiz.question: How does Swiggy's auto-assignment differ from Uber-style dispatch?
options: Instamart is structurally different from food delivery. (1) Dark stores: pre-positioned inventory at ~500 dark stores nationwide, each ~1 500–3 000 SKUs, located in dense neighborhoods.
The KDS exposes a real-time dashboard (per-station queue depth, prep time SLA, station idle time).
The order service is the single source of truth for the order state machine.
Uber asks one driver at a time and waits for explicit accept/reject (driver-pickup model).
quiz.explanation: Uber asks one driver at a time and waits for explicit accept/reject (driver-pickup model). Swiggy's Dispatch 2.0 uses auto-assignment: the system picks the best rider based on (ETA, on-time %, idle time, batch compatibility) and assigns — the rider gets a 15-second window to acknowledge (not accept). If they don't ack, the system moves to the next candidate.

quiz.explanation: Surge service consumes order-placed (demand) and rider-online (supply) Kafka streams over a 5-minute sliding window per H3 hexagon (level 8, ~0.7 km²). demand = orders_in_window, supply = avg_online_riders. Multiplier M = clamp(1.0 + 0.5 * log2(demand/supply), 1.0, 2.5) if demand > supply, else 1.0. To prevent thrash, the per-minute delta is capped at ±0.2× and hysteresis requires a 0.1× change to publish.

Instamart's architecture is simpler than restaurant delivery — no dispatch, no restaurant-accept state.

Three layers. (1) Client-side batching: the rider app batches pings every 5 s and sends them in a single HTTPS request (5 pings per request) — reduces request count 5×.
quiz.explanation: Three layers. (1) Client-side batching: the rider app batches pings every 5 s and sends them in a single HTTPS request (5 pings per request) — reduces request count 5×. (2) Ingestion service with pipelined Redis writes: the ingestion service receives pings, validates, and writes to Redis GEO via pipelined GEOADD (batches of 100 commands per pipeline round-trip).
